topics.title: Piltdown Man: The Greatest Fossil Hoax

hook.text: For 40 years, scientists believed a skull found in England was the missing link between apes and humans. It was a fake.

buildup.text: In 1912, Charles Dawson presented a skull from Piltdown, Sussex. It had a human-sized brain and an ape-like jaw.

discovery.text: Fluorine dating in 1953 proved the jaw was a modern orangutan's, stained and filed to look old.

twist.text: No one has ever proven who did it. Dawson is the prime suspect, but Arthur Conan Doyle — Sherlock Holmes's creator — is.

climax.text: Piltdown Man delayed real human evolution research by decades.

punchline.text: A filed orangutan jaw fooled science for 40 years.

quiz.question: What damage did the Piltdown Man hoax cause?
options: It caused museums worldwide to close their anthropology departments
It delayed real human evolution research and caused scientists to ignore genuine African fossils
It led to a permanent ban on amateur fossil hunting in England

hook.text: A Swedish farmer in Minnesota found a stone with Viking runes in 1898.

buildup.text: The inscription describes 30 explorers who left 10 men by the sea and found them dead and red with blood when they.

discovery.text: Linguists quickly pointed out that the runes used modern Scandinavian grammar, not medieval Norse forms.

twist.text: True believers argue that known Viking exploration of North America makes the stone plausible.

climax.text: Most scholars consider it a 19th-century forgery by Scandinavian immigrants proud of their heritage.

punchline.text: Vikings did reach America — just not Minnesota. Pride carved the rest.

quiz.question: What linguistic evidence suggests the Kensington Runestone is a forgery?
options: The runes are Egyptian hieroglyphs, not Norse writing
The inscription uses modern Scandinavian grammar, not medieval Norse forms
The stone contains English words mixed in with the runes

topics.title: The Cardiff Giant: A Stone Man Hoax

hook.text: Workers digging a well in Cardiff, New York, in 1869 unearthed a 10-foot-tall petrified man. Thousands paid to see it.

buildup.text: George Hull, a cigar maker, had secretly carved the figure from gypsum and buried it a year earlier to win a bet about.

discovery.text: P.T. Barnum offered to buy it. When refused, he made his own fake and claimed Hull's was the copy.

twist.text: Scientists quickly declared it a fake — chisel marks were visible, and gypsum doesn't preserve human tissue.

climax.text: Hull confessed, but the giant kept drawing crowds. People wanted to believe. Admission fees made everyone rich.

punchline.text: The faker confessed. The public kept paying to see it anyway.

quiz.question: What happened after the Cardiff Giant was exposed as a hoax?
options: George Hull was arrested and imprisoned for fraud
People kept paying to see it anyway — wonder beat truth
The sculpture was destroyed by an angry mob

hook.text: The Louvre bought a golden tiara in 1896 for 200,000 francs, calling it a masterpiece of ancient Greek goldwork.

buildup.text: The tiara depicted scenes from Homer's Iliad in exquisite detail.

discovery.text: A Russian goldsmith named Israel Rouchomovsky came forward in 1903 and said he had made it.

twist.text: The Louvre had ignored warnings from scholars who spotted anachronistic details.

climax.text: The scandal embarrassed France's greatest museum and led to stricter authentication procedures worldwide.

punchline.text: The Louvre paid a fortune for a tiara made by a living craftsman.

quiz.question: How was the Tiara of Saitaphernes exposed as a forgery?
options: Chemical analysis proved the gold was mined in modern Russia
The Russian goldsmith who made it came forward and demonstrated his technique
X-rays revealed a hidden message inside the metalwork

hook.text: A Japanese archaeologist discovered one stunning site after another for 30 years. His colleagues called him 'God Hand.'

buildup.text: Shinichi Fujimura pushed Japan's human occupation back to 700,000 years. Textbooks were rewritten.

discovery.text: In 2000, a newspaper photographer hid a camera and filmed Fujimura burying artifacts at a site before the official.

twist.text: He had planted fake artifacts at dozens of sites over three decades.

climax.text: Fujimura confessed and blamed mental illness. His fabrications affected 180 sites and erased decades of published.

punchline.text: God Hand was caught on camera. Thirty years of faked history crumbled.

quiz.question: How was Shinichi Fujimura caught?
options: Radiocarbon dating proved his artifacts were modern
A newspaper photographer secretly filmed him burying artifacts before excavation
A rival archaeologist found the same type of artifact for sale online

hook.text: The Met in New York proudly displayed three giant Etruscan warrior statues for decades.

buildup.text: The terracotta warriors were bought between 1915 and 1921. They were displayed as masterpieces of ancient Italian art.

discovery.text: In 1961, one of the forgers confessed. He proved the fakes were his by producing the missing thumb of one warrior.

twist.text: Art historians had praised the sculptures' 'archaic power.' They saw what they wanted to see — ancient greatness.

climax.text: Thermoluminescence testing, developed later, now catches ceramic fakes.

punchline.text: He kept the thumb for 40 years — the proof that masterpieces can be made.

quiz.question: How did the forger prove the Etruscan warriors were his?
options: He provided the original sketches and designs for each figure
He produced the missing thumb of one warrior that had been lost for decades
He recreated an identical warrior on live television

hook.text: A 600-year-old book written in an unknown script with drawings of unidentifiable plants has defeated every codebreaker.

buildup.text: The Voynich Manuscript has 240 pages of flowing script, botanical illustrations, star charts.

discovery.text: Radiocarbon dating places the vellum at 1404-1438 CE. The ink is consistent with the period. It is genuinely old.

twist.text: Statistical analysis shows the text has linguistic structure — word lengths and patterns resemble natural language.

climax.text: NSA codebreakers, WWII cryptographers, and AI algorithms have all failed.

punchline.text: Six hundred years and the best codebreakers in history. Nobody can read it.

quiz.question: What does statistical analysis suggest about the Voynich Manuscript's text?
options: It is completely random with no linguistic structure at all
Its word patterns resemble natural language, not gibberish
It is written in a simple substitution cipher based on Latin

hook.text: The Minoans of Crete wrote in a script called Linear A. Over 1,400 inscriptions survive.

buildup.text: Linear B — a later script — was deciphered in 1952 and proved to be an early form of Greek.

discovery.text: Scholars can read the numbers and ideograms but not the language.

twist.text: The Minoan language is an isolate — unrelated to any known language.

climax.text: AI and computational linguistics are now tackling Linear A. Patterns are emerging, but no breakthrough has come yet.

punchline.text: We can count their sheep but not read their words.

quiz.question: Why is Linear A so difficult to decipher?
options: Only three inscriptions have been found so far
The Minoan language is unrelated to any known language, and no bilingual text exists
The script was intentionally designed as a secret code

hook.text: The Indus civilization was one of the largest in the ancient world — and we cannot read a single thing they wrote.

buildup.text: Over 4,000 inscriptions survive on seals, tablets, and pottery from Mohenjo-daro and Harappa, dating to 2600-1900 BCE.

discovery.text: The inscriptions are short — averaging five symbols. This may mean they are names, titles, or labels.

twist.text: Some scholars argue it is not writing at all — just symbols like modern logos.

climax.text: Until the script is decoded, the Indus civilization remains the least understood major ancient society on earth.

punchline.text: Five million people. Four thousand inscriptions. Zero translations.

quiz.question: Why is the Indus Valley script so hard to decode?
options: All inscriptions were deliberately erased by later conquerors
Inscriptions are very short — averaging five symbols — and may not be full sentences
The script uses over 10,000 different symbols

hook.text: Easter Island has a writing system that no other Pacific culture developed. Only 26 surviving tablets exist.

buildup.text: Rongorongo glyphs show humans, animals, plants, and geometric shapes carved into wooden boards in a boustrophedon.

discovery.text: Missionaries in the 1860s recorded that only a few chiefs could read the script. Slave raids killed most of them.

twist.text: Some scholars believe Rongorongo was independently invented — one of only a handful of times writing was invented from.

climax.text: With so few tablets and no living readers, decipherment may never be possible.

punchline.text: A tiny island invented writing independently.

quiz.question: Why can't Rongorongo be deciphered?
options: The wooden tablets have decayed beyond recognition
Only 26 tablets survive, and slave raids killed the last people who could read it
It is written in invisible ink that only appears under certain light

hook.text: A clay disc found in Crete has 241 symbols stamped in a spiral pattern. It may be the world's first printed document.

buildup.text: The Phaistos Disc was found in 1908 at the Minoan palace of Phaistos.

discovery.text: The symbols include a helmeted head, a walking man, a cat, an eagle, and a ship — but what they mean is unknown.

twist.text: Some experts believe it is not Minoan at all — the symbols do not match any known Cretan script. It may be foreign.

climax.text: Over 100 decipherment attempts have been published. None has been accepted.

punchline.text: A hundred people claimed to decode it. Zero convinced anyone.

quiz.question: What makes the Phaistos Disc technologically significant?
options: It is the oldest known use of metal for writing
Its symbols were pressed with movable stamps — possibly the first printed document
It contains a mathematical formula for calculating pi

hook.text: One of the world's oldest writing systems — Proto-Elamite from Iran — was used for only 200 years and then abandoned.

buildup.text: Proto-Elamite appeared around 3000 BCE in southwestern Iran. About 1,600 tablets survive, mostly accounting records.

discovery.text: The numbers can be read — they are similar to Mesopotamian systems. The signs next to the numbers remain a mystery.

twist.text: Many tablets contain errors — as if scribes were not fully trained.

climax.text: Oxford's CDLI project has put high-resolution images online, inviting anyone to try cracking it.

punchline.text: They invented writing, got confused by their own system.

quiz.question: Why was Proto-Elamite possibly abandoned?
options: A conquering army banned all writing in the region
The system may have been too complex — tablets show scribal errors suggesting poor training
A new religion declared writing to be sacrilegious

topics.title: The Nazca Lines: Drawings for the Gods

hook.text: Giant drawings of animals and shapes stretch across the Peruvian desert.

buildup.text: The Nazca people created them between 500 BCE and 500 CE by removing red pebbles to expose lighter ground underneath.

discovery.text: Pilot Toribio Mejía Xesspe spotted them from the air in 1927. Hummingbirds, monkeys, spiders.

twist.text: You do not need to fly to make them. Studies proved they can be planned from the ground using simple stakes and string.

climax.text: The lines may have been ritual paths walked during ceremonies, pointing toward water sources in the dry desert.

punchline.text: No aliens needed. Stakes, string, and faith built drawings visible from space.

quiz.question: How were the Nazca Lines likely created?
options: With advanced aerial surveying equipment now lost to history
Using simple stakes and string to plan from the ground
By following natural geological patterns already in the rock

hook.text: A corroded lump from a Roman shipwreck turned out to be the most complex mechanism built by the ancient world.

buildup.text: Found in 1901 off Antikythera, Greece, the device had over 30 interlocking bronze gears hidden inside a wooden box.

discovery.text: It predicted eclipses, tracked the Moon's irregular orbit, and even calculated the dates of the Olympic Games.

twist.text: Nothing remotely this complex was made again until European clockmakers in the 1300s.

climax.text: CT scans in 2006 revealed tiny inscriptions — an instruction manual.

punchline.text: Greeks built an analog computer 2,000 years ago.

quiz.question: What is most astonishing about the Antikythera Mechanism?
options: It was powered by steam, predating the Industrial Revolution
Nothing this complex was built again until European clockmakers 1,400 years later
It was found intact and in perfect working condition

topics.title: The Plain of Jars: Laos's Stone Puzzle

hook.text: Thousands of giant stone jars — some weighing 14 tons — are scattered across a plain in Laos. No one knows why.

buildup.text: The jars are carved from sandstone, granite, and limestone. They stand up to 10 feet tall and date to around 500 BCE to.

discovery.text: Some jars contained human bones, teeth, glass beads, and bronze tools. They were likely used in burial rituals.

twist.text: The plain is one of the most heavily bombed places on earth. U.S.

climax.text: UNESCO declared it a World Heritage Site in 2019. Bomb clearance teams must clear unexploded ordnance before.

punchline.text: Ancient mystery meets modern danger. You need a bomb squad before you can dig.

quiz.question: What modern danger complicates research on the Plain of Jars?
options: Frequent earthquakes collapse the jars and threaten researchers
Unexploded bombs from the Vietnam War make excavation extremely dangerous
Illegal mining operations have destroyed most of the site

topics.title: The Bog Bodies: Preserved in Peat

hook.text: Bodies thousands of years old lie in European bogs with skin, hair, and fingernails perfectly preserved.

buildup.text: Peat bogs are acidic and oxygen-free — perfect for preservation.

discovery.text: Tollund Man, found in Denmark in 1950, looks like he is sleeping. He was hanged around 400 BCE.

twist.text: Many bog bodies show signs of ritual killing — stabbing, strangling, and drowning.

climax.text: Grauballe Man's last meal was a porridge of 60 different plant species — perhaps a ritual recipe prepared for his death.

punchline.text: They killed them, fed them a special meal, and dropped them in a bog.

quiz.question: Why are bog bodies so well preserved?
options: Ancient embalming techniques were used before burial
Peat bogs are acidic and oxygen-free — perfect conditions for preservation
Cold temperatures in Northern Europe freeze organic material indefinitely

topics.title: Göbekli Tepe: The Temple Before Farming

hook.text: Hunter-gatherers in Turkey built a monumental stone temple 11,600 years ago — 6,000 years before Stonehenge and before.

buildup.text: Göbekli Tepe has massive T-shaped pillars carved with lions, foxes, scorpions, and vultures. The largest weigh 10 tons.

discovery.text: Klaus Schmidt began excavating in 1995 and found multiple enclosures intentionally buried by their builders.

twist.text: It overturned the theory that farming came before religion. At Göbekli Tepe.

climax.text: Only 5 percent of the site has been excavated. The rest lies buried, deliberately preserved by its original builders.

punchline.text: They built a temple before they grew crops.

quiz.question: How did Göbekli Tepe change our understanding of civilization?
options: It proved that agriculture was invented in Turkey, not the Fertile Crescent
It showed that religion and monumental building may have preceded farming
It demonstrated that stone tools were invented much earlier than believed

topics.title: The Copper Scroll: A Real Treasure Map

hook.text: Among the Dead Sea Scrolls was a copper sheet listing 64 locations where gold and silver are supposedly hidden.

buildup.text: Found in 1952 at Qumran, the Copper Scroll is unique among the Dead Sea Scrolls — it is not religious but a practical.

discovery.text: The locations use landmarks that no longer exist: 'in the gutter under the east wall,' 'in the cistern under.

twist.text: Many expeditions have searched the listed locations. No treasure has ever been found.

climax.text: Some scholars believe the treasure was Jerusalem's Temple wealth hidden before the Roman invasion of 70 CE.

punchline.text: A 2,000-year-old treasure map with 64 locations. Not one ounce has been found.

quiz.question: What might the Copper Scroll's treasure represent?
options: Pirate treasure from Mediterranean raiders
Jerusalem's Temple wealth hidden before the Roman invasion of 70 CE
Offerings collected by the Essene community at Qumran

topics.title: The Roanoke Colony: The Lost Colonists

hook.text: In 1590, a ship returned to Roanoke Island to find 115 English colonists gone.

buildup.text: The colony was established in 1587 on the coast of present-day North Carolina.

discovery.text: War with Spain delayed White's return by three years. When he arrived, every building had been dismantled and.

twist.text: Croatoan was the name of a nearby island where friendly Native Americans lived.

climax.text: DNA studies and recent archaeological digs suggest the colonists integrated into local tribes.

punchline.text: They were not lost. They moved in with the neighbors.

quiz.question: What do recent studies suggest happened to the Roanoke colonists?
options: They were killed in a conflict with Spanish soldiers
They integrated into local Native American tribes rather than perishing
They built boats and sailed back to England on their own

hook.text: Europe's first great civilization — the Minoans of Crete — built grand palaces and then suddenly disappeared around.

buildup.text: The Minoans had flushing toilets, multi-story buildings, and vibrant art. They dominated the Aegean for over 500 years.

discovery.text: The volcanic eruption of Thera around 1600 BCE devastated the region.

twist.text: The final destruction came 150 years after Thera — meaning the eruption weakened them but something else finished.

climax.text: Mycenaean Greeks from the mainland took over Crete around 1450 BCE.

punchline.text: A volcano weakened them. Greeks finished them.

quiz.question: What likely caused the final end of Minoan civilization?
options: The Thera eruption destroyed all their palaces in a single day
Mycenaean Greeks conquered Crete about 150 years after the Thera eruption
A plague carried by Egyptian traders wiped out the population

hook.text: Around 1200 BCE, almost every great civilization in the eastern Mediterranean collapsed within a single generation.

buildup.text: The Hittites, Mycenaeans, Egyptians, Assyrians, and Canaanites all fell or were severely weakened between 1250 and 1150.

discovery.text: Letters from the period describe mysterious 'Sea Peoples' raiding coastlines.

twist.text: No single cause has been proven. Drought, earthquakes, trade disruption, internal revolts.

climax.text: It was history's first systems collapse — interconnected societies that were too dependent on each other to survive.

punchline.text: An entire world order collapsed in one generation. It took 400 years to rebuild.

quiz.question: What made the Bronze Age Collapse so devastating?
options: A single massive earthquake destroyed every major city simultaneously
Interconnected societies were too dependent on each other — when one fell, all fell
A new religion spread rapidly and caused all kingdoms to abandon their capitals

topics.title: The Ancestral Puebloans: Cliff Dwellers Who Left

hook.text: The Ancestral Puebloans built stunning cliff dwellings at Mesa Verde — then abandoned them all around 1300 CE and never.

buildup.text: Their cliff palaces had hundreds of rooms, towers, and kivas carved into sandstone overhangs in the American Southwest.

discovery.text: Tree-ring data shows a severe drought hit the region from 1276 to 1299 — the Great Drought devastated agriculture.

twist.text: Drought was not the only factor. Evidence of warfare, burned villages, and even cannibalism suggests social collapse.

climax.text: They did not vanish — they migrated south and became today's Pueblo peoples: Hopi, Zuni, and Rio Grande communities.

punchline.text: They were not lost. They left a home that could no longer feed them.

quiz.question: What happened to the Ancestral Puebloans of Mesa Verde?
options: They were wiped out by European diseases before Columbus arrived
They migrated south and became today's Pueblo peoples: Hopi, Zuni, and others
They moved into underground cities that have never been found

topics.title: The Khmer Empire: Angkor's Slow Decline

hook.text: The Khmer Empire built Angkor Wat and ruled Southeast Asia for 600 years. Then the jungle swallowed their capital.

buildup.text: At its peak, Angkor was the largest pre-industrial city on earth — a million people supported by a vast water.

discovery.text: LiDAR revealed the true extent of Angkor in 2012: a sprawling urban landscape extending far beyond the temple complex.

twist.text: Climate studies show severe droughts in the 14th and 15th centuries destroyed Angkor's water system.

climax.text: Thai invasions delivered the final blow in 1431. But the collapse was already underway.

punchline.text: The world's largest city ran on water. When the rain stopped, so did the empire.

quiz.question: What was the primary cause of Angkor's decline?
options: A plague carried along trade routes from China
Severe droughts destroyed the water management system the city depended on
Internal religious conflict led to civil war and abandonment

topics.title: The Greenland Norse: Vikings Who Vanished

hook.text: Vikings settled Greenland in 985 CE and thrived for 500 years. By the 1400s, they were gone. No one knows exactly why.

buildup.text: The Norse established farms, churches, and trade routes. At their peak, about 5,000 people lived in two settlements.

discovery.text: Excavations show they raised cattle and sheep but refused to eat fish or learn Inuit hunting methods — a fatal cultural.

twist.text: The Little Ice Age cooled Greenland severely. Sea ice blocked trade ships.

climax.text: The last known record is a 1408 wedding. After that, silence. No graves of the final settlers have ever been found.

punchline.text: They farmed in a place meant for hunting. The ice returned and the ships.

quiz.question: What cultural failure contributed to the Greenland Norse collapse?
options: They converted to a religion that forbade them from eating land animals
They refused to eat fish or learn Inuit hunting methods despite worsening conditions
They waged constant war against neighboring Inuit settlements

topics.title: Ancient Aliens: Why the Theory Is Wrong

hook.text: A popular TV show claims aliens built the pyramids, Nazca Lines, and Stonehenge.

buildup.text: Ancient alien claims argue that ancient peoples were too 'primitive' to build their own monuments.

discovery.text: We have the tools, quarries, construction ramps, and worker villages for the pyramids.

twist.text: The theory is rooted in racism. It implies non-European peoples needed alien help — but no one claims aliens built.

climax.text: Ancient peoples were intelligent, creative, and capable. Denying their achievements insults their legacy.

punchline.text: Humans built it all. The real mystery is why some people cannot accept that.

quiz.question: What underlying bias do scholars identify in ancient alien theories?
options: They are funded by governments to distract from real archaeological discoveries
They imply non-European peoples needed alien help — a fundamentally racist assumption
They are based on misinterpretations of sacred religious texts

topics.title: Atlantis: The Myth That Won't Die

hook.text: Plato described a powerful island civilization that sank beneath the sea.

buildup.text: Plato placed Atlantis beyond the Pillars of Hercules, describing a ringed city with advanced technology that angered.

discovery.text: Atlantis has been 'found' in Spain, Morocco, Antarctica, the Bahamas, Sardinia, and the eye of the Sahara.

twist.text: Plato likely invented the story as a philosophical parable about hubris and divine punishment — not a historical.

climax.text: The Thera eruption and destruction of Minoan Crete may have inspired the legend — a real civilization destroyed by.

punchline.text: A philosopher invented a moral story. The world spent 2,400 years looking for.

quiz.question: What is the most likely explanation for Plato's Atlantis story?
options: It was based on a lost Egyptian map found in Alexandria's library
It was a philosophical parable about hubris, possibly inspired by the Minoan collapse
It was a coded message describing the location of real treasure

hook.text: Life-size crystal skulls were sold as ancient Aztec or Maya artifacts. Indiana Jones featured them.

buildup.text: Several crystal skulls appeared in collections in the late 1800s.

discovery.text: Electron microscope analysis showed tool marks from modern rotary grinding wheels — technology unavailable to ancient.

twist.text: The crystal likely came from Madagascar or Brazil. No crystal skull has ever been found in a documented archaeological.

climax.text: The British Museum and Smithsonian both tested their skulls and concluded they were 19th-century European fakes.

punchline.text: No ancient origin. No mystical powers. Just clever 19th-century craftsmen and.

quiz.question: How did scientists prove crystal skulls are modern?
options: Radiocarbon dating placed the crystal at less than 200 years old
Electron microscopes revealed tool marks from modern rotary grinding wheels
Chemical analysis showed the crystal was synthetic, not natural quartz

hook.text: When Lord Carnarvon died weeks after opening Tutankhamun's tomb, newspapers blamed an ancient curse.

buildup.text: Carnarvon died of an infected mosquito bite in April 1923. Reporters claimed lights went out in Cairo at the exact.

discovery.text: Howard Carter, who actually opened the tomb and spent years inside it, lived until 1939 — perfectly healthy at age 64.

twist.text: A study of 25 people present at the opening found they lived an average of 20 more years.

climax.text: Some scientists suggest toxic mold spores in sealed tombs could cause illness — a natural hazard.

punchline.text: The man who opened the tomb lived 16 more years.

quiz.question: What does statistical analysis show about the 'pharaoh's curse'?
options: People present at the tomb opening died significantly younger than average
The 25 people present lived an average of 20 more years — no curse effect
Only those who touched artifacts directly showed signs of illness

hook.text: Lost continents, ancient energy grids, and giant civilizations — pseudoarchaeology thrives because real archaeology.

buildup.text: Pseudoarchaeological claims ignore evidence, cherry-pick data, and present speculation as fact.

discovery.text: Common red flags: unnamed experts, no published research, claims that mainstream science is hiding the truth.

twist.text: Pseudoarchaeology often exploits real gaps in knowledge. Genuine mysteries attract fake explanations because real.

climax.text: The best defense is scientific literacy: checking sources, reading peer-reviewed papers.

punchline.text: If the explanation is exciting and requires no evidence, it is probably wrong.

quiz.question: What is a key red flag of pseudoarchaeological claims?
options: They are published in university journals
They claim mainstream science is hiding the truth and skip peer review
They focus on well-documented periods of history

topics.title: Graham Hancock and the Lost Civilization

hook.text: A bestselling author claims an advanced civilization existed during the Ice Age and was wiped out.

buildup.text: Graham Hancock argues that Göbekli Tepe, the Sphinx, and underwater ruins prove a lost global civilization existed.

discovery.text: His Netflix show 'Ancient Apocalypse' reached millions. Archaeologists called it the most dangerous show on television.

twist.text: Hancock accuses archaeologists of a cover-up. In reality, scholars publish all findings openly and welcome challenges —.

climax.text: The appeal is emotional: a mystery bigger than experts admit. But extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence —.

punchline.text: Millions of viewers, zero peer-reviewed papers. Popularity is not proof.

quiz.question: Why do archaeologists criticize Graham Hancock's claims?
options: He refuses to visit any archaeological sites in person
His claims lack peer-reviewed evidence and accuse scholars of a cover-up
He only focuses on European sites and ignores the rest of the world
